items.question: What practice must accompany worship of this circle to produce its effect?
items.inference: Worship of the circle must be sustained by continuous meditation.
items.plain_english: Having worshipped this circle, one applies meditation for as long as one continues the practice.

items.question: What kinds of languages become perceptible through this meditative practice?
items.inference: The practice grants perception of diverse languages, both familiar and unfamiliar.
uncertainties: Gender agreement between bhāṣās (f.) and aśrutāni/śrutāni (n.) is taken as referring to utterances or forms.
items.plain_english: Indeed, languages of various forms are heard, both those never heard before and those already heard.

items.question: Where and by whom are these languages heard in the yogic experience?
premises: The self is agent, recipient, and locus
items.inference: The languages are heard entirely within and by the practitioner's own self.
items.plain_english: Indeed, they are heard by oneself alone, by the self, to the self, and within the self.

items.question: What bodily transformation results from the described yogic attainment?
premises: The practitioner becomes free of wrinkles and grey hair
The resemblance is as a second Kāma
items.inference: The attainment yields a rejuvenated, divinely beautiful body like a second god of love.
items.plain_english: Freed from wrinkles and grey hair, he becomes like a second god of love.

rows.grounds: source or force to be destroyed; compound vāyu+ādi
simile for resulting state; compound mūka+vat

items.question: What effect on speech can be produced by destroying the force of wind and related powers?
premises: The force of wind and others is destroyed by speech
The affected person remains like a mute
The state is one of standing speechless
items.inference: Destroying the wind-related force by mantra renders the target mute.
uncertainties: The exact referent of vāyvādeḥ (wind element, breath, or hostile force) is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: By destroying the force of wind and the rest through speech, he indeed stands like a mute.

rows.grounds: function of the circle; compound sainya+stambha+kara

items.question: What supreme power is attributed to the seventh circle addressed to the goddess?
premises: It is addressed to the goddess
items.inference: The seventh circle is a supreme means for paralyzing armies.
items.plain_english: O Goddess, the seventh circle is supreme and causes the paralysis of armies.

rows.grounds: practitioner devoted to pūjā and dhyāna; compound pūjā+dhyāna+rata

items.question: What perceptual capacity arises for one devoted to worship and meditation on that circle?
premises: The practitioner is devoted to worship and meditation
items.inference: Devotion to worship and meditation on that circle grants distant vision.
items.plain_english: Indeed, for one devoted to worship and meditation on that circle, vision arises even from afar.

items.question: Which hostile and coercive powers become available through this circle's application?
items.inference: The circle enables killing, uprooting, paralyzing, deluding, and related powers.
items.plain_english: O fortunate one, O beloved, killing, uprooting, paralyzing, deluding, and such powers become possible.

rows.grounds: ritual or doctrinal arrangement; compound aṣṭa+aṣṭaka+vidhāna

items.question: What knowledge is required for success in the eightfold-eight method?
premises: The eight-times-eight method must be known
items.inference: Success in this method depends exclusively on knowing the eight-times-eight arrangement.
items.plain_english: Indeed, having known the method of the eight groups of eight, one succeeds; not otherwise.

items.question: How should the declared teaching be ascertained without doubt by the practitioner?
premises: The teaching is declared without doubt
items.inference: The teaching is to be firmly ascertained through both devotion and reasoning.
uncertainties: avadhāram may function as a verbal noun or object of an implied action.
items.plain_english: Indeed, this has been declared by me without doubt; ascertain it with devotion and reasoning.

rows.grounds: locative title of text section; compound candradvīpa+vinirgata

items.question: Which chapter concludes in the text emerged from Candradvīpa?
premises: The text is identified as emerged from Candradvīpa
items.inference: This marks the eighth chapter in the Candradvīpa-emerged text.
items.plain_english: In the text emerged from Candradvīpa, this is the eighth chapter.

rows.grounds: topic to be explained; compound yoginī+pañkti+vinyāsa

items.question: What teaching does the speaker promise to explain to the beloved listener next?
premises: The topic is the arrangement of yoginī rows
items.inference: The speaker will now explain the arrangement of the rows of yoginīs.
items.plain_english: O beloved, I shall tell you the arrangement of the rows of yoginīs.

rows.grounds: collective group of yoginīs; compound sarva+bhūcarī+sarva+gocara+yoginī
total domain or field; compound sarva+kṣetraka

items.question: What total domain encompasses all earth-moving and sky-moving yoginīs?
premises: They belong to a complete field-group
items.inference: The complete field-group comprises all earth-moving and all sky-moving yoginīs.
uncertainties: The syntactic role of sarvakṣetrakam in the larger sentence is incomplete in this verse alone.
items.plain_english: The entire field-group of all earth-moving and all sky-moving yoginīs.

items.question: Which classes of yoginīs are enumerated as part of this arrangement?
items.inference: The arrangement includes innate, family-born, and door-guardian yoginīs.
uncertainties: sarvakulajā appears singular in form but is read as plural in this list context.
items.plain_english: All the innate ones, all those born of the families, and all the door-guardians.

items.question: Why has the supreme secret among secrets been revealed to the listener?
premises: The teaching is the supreme secret of secrets
The revelation is due to the listener's devotion
items.inference: The supreme secret is revealed because of the listener's devotion.
items.plain_english: Because of your devotion, the supreme secret of secrets has been revealed.

items.question: What instruction does the listener now wish to hear from the gurus?
premises: The listener expresses a present wish
The wish is to hear from the gurus
The topic is the worship of the siddhas
items.inference: The listener now wishes to hear from the gurus about the worship of the siddhas.
items.plain_english: Now I wish to hear from the gurus about the worship of the siddhas.

items.question: To whom should the arrangement of the two syllables be imparted?
items.inference: The two-syllable arrangement should be imparted to others as prescribed.
uncertainties: The exact meaning of anyanteṣu is unclear without broader context.
items.plain_english: One should impart the arrangement of the two syllables to others.

rows.grounds: negation of past or present equivalent

items.question: What unique status is claimed for this knowledge compared to all other knowledge?
premises: No knowledge equal to this exists
No equal knowledge will arise again
items.inference: This knowledge is declared uniquely unsurpassed in past and future.
items.plain_english: There is no knowledge equal to this, nor will there ever be again.

items.question: What does the speaker promise to explain regarding the names of those beings?
premises: The speaker addresses the listener directly
The topic is the method of their names
items.inference: The speaker will explain the method or procedure of their names.
items.plain_english: O beautiful-eyed one, listen: I shall speak the method of their names.

items.question: Who are identified as the independent impellers of the lineage across the four ages?
premises: They are impellers of the family or lineage
items.inference: The independent impellers of the lineage are identified in relation to the four ages.
uncertainties: The precise syntactic relation of caturyuga iti to the rest of the verse is compressed.
items.plain_english: O Lord of gods, thus are the independent impellers of the lineage, called the Four Ages.

items.question: What is the extent and origin of this Kaula teaching?
premises: The teaching is identified as Kaula
It is arisen from the supreme
items.inference: This Kaula teaching is vast in extent and originates from the supreme.
uncertainties: The unit implied by daśakoṭi (verses, mantras, or beings) is not specified.
items.plain_english: Indeed, this Kaula teaching, arisen from the supreme, measures ten crores.

items.question: By what power and up to what limit does the yoginī named Will operate with the siddhas?
premises: A yoginī named Icchā is identified
She is associated with the siddhas
Her operation extends up to māyā by supreme will
items.inference: The yoginī Icchā, with the siddhas, operates up to the limit of māyā by supreme will.
uncertainties: The verbal action governing māyāntaṃ is implicit in this verse.
items.plain_english: The yoginī named Icchā, together with the siddhas, extends up to māyā by the supreme will.

items.question: To whom was this teaching transmitted again by the sky-moving beings?
items.inference: The sky-movers transmitted the teaching again to the mothers.
items.plain_english: O goddess, O beloved, it was told again to the mothers by the sky-movers.

items.question: Who transmitted the teaching to the earth-moving beings described as good eaters?
premises: They are described as good eaters
items.inference: An earth-moving being transmitted the teaching to the earth-moving beings, the good eaters.
uncertainties: The distinction between singular bhūcarī as agent and plural bhūcarīṇāṃ as recipients is preserved as given.
items.plain_english: O beloved, it was told to the earth-moving beings, the good eaters, by an earth-mover.
